judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard consideration/insuring preamble; no term in it carries competing meanings and nothing turns on its boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the declarations and 'all the terms of this policy,' which sits comfortably with Condition 12 (Declarations) and the endorsement attachment clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed enumerated list of supplementary payments with fixed dollar caps; the items are specific and the '$250 per bail bond'/'$25 per day' figures are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly amended by the HPL First Aid Exclusion (c049), the prejudgment-interest endorsement (c169) and the nuclear exclusion (c199), so its residual scope depends on reconciling three later texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare definitional preamble with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the definitions apply to endorsements too, which matters where endorsements redefine terms (c195 products hazard, c162 occurrence), but the redefinitions are express.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard 'automobile' definition keyed to a clear carve-out for mobile equipment; boundaries are drawn by cross-reference rather than left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with the 'mobile equipment' definition (c012) and the loading/unloading definition (c168) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Bodily injury ... which occurs during the policy period' is the classic trigger phrase, and 'occurs' is genuinely contestable for latent or continuing injury.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition is expanded by the Incidental Medical Malpractice coverage (c158) and by Extended Bodily Injury (c162), and HPL instead triggers on a 'medical incident which occurs during the policy period' (c038), so the two trigger tests must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long technical definition; the only wobble is the stray 'incident contract' for 'incidental contract', which a court would read as an obvious slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It keys to the completed operations and underground property damage hazards, which are defined consistently in c007 and c019.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard completed-operations definition with enumerated completion times and carve-outs; specific rather than open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the products hazard (c017) and the redefinition endorsement (c195), which only alters products hazard, leaving this text intact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated 'elevator' definition with express exclusions; the four-foot dumbwaiter cutoff is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used in exclusion (l) (c125) and in the Broad Form property damage carve-outs (c156), consistently in each place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Technical hazard definition with numbered exceptions; nothing vague, though 'incidemal contract' is a typo for a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with exclusion (q)'s classification-symbol scheme (c130) and the incidental contract definition (c010).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five written contract types, the paradigm setting for expressio unius arguments about what is left out; the numbering is also garbled ('(3) lease' then '(3) undertaking').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form endorsement (c135/c136 context) expressly extends 'incidental contract' to any oral or written contract relating to the named insured's business, which materially conflicts with this narrow list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The insurance afforded applies separately to each insured ... except with respect to the limits' is a severability clause whose interaction with exclusions is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether severability defeats exclusions written 'any insured' (e.g. c144, c190) and how it meshes with the single aggregate in c044 is a real whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long enumerated definition of mobile equipment; specific categories rather than a vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors and cross-limits the automobile definition (c004) and is used in exclusions (c) and (d) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Named insured means the person or organization named in Item 1' is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Additional Named Insureds form (c092) and Endorsement 13 (c211) add a dozen further named insureds, so 'named insured' in Item 1 does not exhaust the class and the singular reference can mislead.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard products definition with an express vending-machine carve-out; the closing clause is convoluted but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Products Hazard Redefined endorsement (c195) narrows the related hazard definition but leaves this one untouched.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured' and 'accident, including continuous or repeated exposure' are among the most-litigated phrases in liability insurance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Extended Bodily Injury Coverage (c162) rewrites 'occurrence' to include some intentional acts, and the HPL part triggers on 'medical incident' (c046) rather than occurrence, leaving two coverage triggers to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb territorial definition; each limb is concrete, and the proviso about suit being brought within the territory is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limited Worldwide Liability (c160) expands it, and the HPL part has its own territory clause (c045) later amended twice (c172, c205), so the operative territory depends on which part is in play.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional products hazard definition; the text is OCR-mangled but the substantive elements are standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Products Hazard Redefined endorsement (c195) deletes the 'away from premises owned or rented' element for scheduled premises/operations, so this definition is partly superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Physical injury to or destruction of tangible property' with a loss-of-use limb is standard; the 'occurs during the policy period' timing element is the only contestable part.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The nuclear endorsement (c201) expands 'property damage' to include radioactive contamination, an express and limited override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical definition with an enumerated property list ('wires, conduits, pipes ... and similar property') followed by a catch-all, which invites ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with exclusion (q)(3) (c130) and the collapse/explosion hazard definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An administrative premium condition tied to the company's own manuals; 'advance premium' and 'earned premium' are defined in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pay Plan endorsement (c113) fixes installments and due dates, which supplements rather than contradicts this computation machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Inspection/audit rights with an express disclaimer; the three-year post-termination audit window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses inspection or audit rights, so there is no competing text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A financial-responsibility conformity clause with a reimbursement undertaking; concrete and conditioned on certification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Amendment—Limits of Liability (c165) contains a parallel financial-responsibility proviso, which is consistent with this condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practicable' notice is a recurrent construction issue, though courts treat it as a familiar reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is expressly replaced twice — by the HPL Amended Condition (c048) and by the Wisconsin amendatory 'as soon as reasonably possible' (c095) — leaving three competing notice standards in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Immediately forward every demand, notice, summons or other process' is specific and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is restated almost verbatim in the HPL amended condition (c048), so the duplication is harmonious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cooperation clause with a voluntary-payment bar; 'cooperate' is broad but is the standard formulation courts apply routinely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded for the HPL part by c048 and the first-aid carve-out is removed by c049, so its residual field must be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-action clause with a condition precedent of 'full compliance with all of the terms'; broad but conventional wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement deletes this condition 'in its entirety' and replaces it (c114), while the Professional Liability Amendatory says the Action Against Company condition 'does not apply' (c098) — three inconsistent treatments of the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Primary insurance, except when stated to apply in excess of or contingent upon the absence of other insurance' is a standard but frequently contested other-insurance formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements make specific coverages excess (c155, c157, c159, c186) and the Overlap Endorsement (c175) adds a further layer, so the primary/excess hierarchy must be assembled from many texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical equal-shares contribution formula; the arithmetic is spelled out step by step.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates only through the introductory Other Insurance text (c027) and the excess endorsements, which expressly amend that condition rather than this sub-part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A proportional contribution-by-limits formula; definite and arithmetically closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same as the equal-shares clause: it is subordinate to c027 and is not contradicted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard subrogation with a cooperation duty; nothing open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin endorsement (c115) adds a make-whole proviso that materially changes when the company may recover, a change that must be read back into this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-waiver/no-oral-change clause; its terms are categorical rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both c096 and c116 rewrite 'Changes' to impute an agent's knowledge to the company, the direct opposite of this clause's first sentence, and two different amended versions coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment consent plus a death-of-named-insured saving provision; specific and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named insured here is a corporation, so the 'shall die' limb is inapt, but nothing else in the policy contradicts the clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional annualisation rule; its own terms are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared policy period is a single year (03/01/1996–03/01/1997), so the condition is dormant, and the Wisconsin cancellation forms separately address multi-year policies (c110).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cancellation mechanic with a stated thirty-day notice figure; the OCR '(20)' beside 'thirty' is a visible discrepancy between word and numeral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 requires sixty days' notice (c069), the Wisconsin cancellation form requires ten days for most mid-term cancellations (c108, c109) and restricts grounds (c099), so the notice period and grounds are governed by at least three inconsistent texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration-plus-representations clause; broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both c097 and c117 add a Wisconsin paragraph neutralising most misrepresentation defences, which substantially cuts against the reliance language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate attachment sentence; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated identically across the endorsements and creates no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlicensed physicians', 'rotate to', and 'do not follow them with their respective coverages' are all imprecise, and 'this coverage with apply' is a mechanical error; whether 'not otherwise' means excess or no coverage is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deems these physicians covered 'as if they were employees', but the Wisconsin Persons Insured clause (c056) excludes physicians licensed under Ch. 448 from the employee class and c058/c183 cover medical staff only for administrative acts, so the deeming provision has to be squared with those limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on 'injury ... caused by a medical incident which occurs during the policy period', and both the trigger and the undefined word 'injury' (not 'bodily injury') are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the 'medical incident' definition (c046), the exhaustion sentence against the aggregate limit (c044), and the declarations' differing aggregate figure, all of which bear on when the duty to defend ends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard employee-injury exclusion; 'arising out of and in the course of employment' is a familiar and workable test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The GL 00 32 endorsement (c170) deletes and replaces 'the exclusion relating to bodily injury to any employee of the insured' without saying whether it reaches this HPL exclusion or only the CGL one, leaving which text governs unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Workers'-compensation-type obligations exclusion with a 'similar law' catch-all after a specific list, a modest ejusdem generis point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the CGL exclusion (i) and the medical payments exclusion (c146)(4) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Liability of an insured, if an individual, for such insured's personal acts or omissions involving a medical incident' is a sweeping and oddly-phrased carve-out whose reach against individual insureds is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is declared inapplicable to the Wisconsin Persons Insured endorsement (c060) and to medical staff performing listed functions (c184), so whether any individual insured remains excluded requires reconciling three texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An auto/watercraft/aircraft exclusion; on its own the wording is standard, though the reproduced text has lost its '(d)' label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-050 (c188) rewrites this exclusion to preserve professional-services coverage and Endorsement 5 (c071) further extends it to loading/unloading patients and air ambulances, so the printed text is superseded twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enumerated Persons Insured list; each category is defined by role and scope of duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-109 WI (c051–c058) states that these provisions 'are changed to read as follows', so this printed list is entirely displaced yet remains in the policy, and further extensions (c091, c183, c197) add classes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'each medical incident' limit is cut off mid-phrase in the text and the aggregate/per-incident interplay depends on the contested single-incident aggregation rule in the medical incident definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state a $4,000,000 aggregate while the coverage-part schedule states $1,000,000, and c173 raises limits to $1M/$3M for non-Fund insureds while c193 makes limits apply separately by entity and c187 forbids increases — a genuine multi-document limits conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The territorial words are literally missing from the clause ('anywhere in the .'), and the suit-location proviso is the operative constraint.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two later endorsements amend HPL Policy Territory (c172, then c205 after c203 deletes the first), so which territorial text governs is a document-wide question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Medical incident' and especially the aggregation sentence — related acts to 'any one person' count as one incident — is precisely the kind of counting rule parties fight over, and 'professional health care services' is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the per-incident limit in c044 and the exclusive-coverage statement in c050, and sits against the CGL's Incidental Medical Malpractice coverage (c158) for overlapping medical acts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow definitional extension of 'suit' to consented arbitration; specific and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form arbitration condition (c137) concerns contractual liability arbitration only, so there is no clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice 'as soon as practicable' of any claim or of 'specific circumstances involving a particular person likely to result in a claim' is a vague reporting trigger that parties commonly dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin amendatory (c095) replaces Condition 4(a) with a 'as soon as reasonably possible' standard for the same professional coverage, so two notice standards govern the same claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence deletion of first-aid expense for this part; clear in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends the Supplementary Payments clause (c002)(c) for the HPL part only, while the CGL Incidental Medical Malpractice provision (c158) contains its own first-aid carve-out, so several parallel amendments exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as stated in this Part, this policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident' is a sweeping negation whose reach across the whole instrument is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It appears to cancel the CGL's Incidental Medical Malpractice Liability Coverage (c158) and to cut against the charitable health care extensions (c090, c196) which extend 'the coverages provided by this policy' to community care.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure amendment instruction; the words 'changed to read as follows' are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It wholly displaces c043 while later endorsements (c091, c183, c197) add further classes to the same provision, so the final Persons Insured text is assembled from several forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble to a list; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'To the extent set forth below' works with the subparagraphs and the later added (f) and (g) categories without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three words identifying the named insured as an insured; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Named insured' is expanded by c092 and c211, but that expansion is express.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional partnership/joint venture clause; conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named insured is designated as a corporation in the declarations, so the limb is dormant and consistent with c059.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of officers and board members limited to acts 'within the scope of his duties as such'; the scope limitation is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with (d) employees and with c058's administrative-duties class, but the categories are cumulative rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause turns on 'permanently practicing in Wisconsin, as such' and on a double-negative proviso about injury to employees, students and volunteers — both are genuinely hard to apply at the margin.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its physician exclusion sits directly against Endorsement 1 (c037), which treats rotating unlicensed physicians as employees, and against c058/c183 covering physicians for administrative acts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Accreditation/board-member class with a 'similar professional board or committee' catch-all after specific examples, a modest general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates in substance the medical incident definition's limb (b) (c046) and the Extension of Persons Insured (c183)(3), which are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Administrative duties, as described in the medical staff bylaws and/or policies and procedures' imports an extrinsic and shifting document, and the administrative/clinical line is the classic dispute for physician-executives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Extension of Persons Insured (c183–c185) covers medical staff for administrative acts but expressly excludes rendering professional health care services, so the two texts must be read together to fix the boundary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short partnership/joint-venture exclusion; its operation is mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the identical CGL clause (c063) and the CGL Persons Insured closing sentence (c131) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line disapplication of Exclusion (c); its own words are clear but it does not say whether it displaces the exclusion generally or only for this endorsement's insureds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (c) (c041) is also disapplied for medical staff by c184, so the exclusion survives only in a residue that has to be derived from three texts.
